`aggregates.<name>.sql` (required): one read-only SELECT that returns one column (a `WITH ... SELECT` or a `VALUES` counts). The value is that column of the first row; no row, or NULL (MAX over no rows), is stored as no value. A statement that returns two columns fails every refresh. Anything else (a statement that writes, a second statement, a PRAGMA, DDL) is refused when app.yaml is written; the statement runs on a read-only connection, so in an app.yaml deployed with one it fails every refresh and changes nothing.

`aggregates.<name>.refresh` (required): how often the value is recomputed, a quoted duration in seconds, minutes or hours: "90s", "5m", "1h", "1h30m". Less than 1m runs every minute and more than 24h every 24 hours. Days ("1d") and a bare number (60) are not durations. An aggregate without a `refresh` that is a duration is refused when app.yaml is written; in an app.yaml deployed with one it is not refreshed and has no value. A key other than `sql` and `refresh` is also refused.
The statement runs as the app, with no viewer: nothing is bound into it (no `:user_id`, no `?`) and no access rule, owner filter or tenant filter applies. Its WHERE clause is the only filter.

SQL that reads an encrypted column is refused when it is written: api({at:'encryption'}) computed_aggregates. A table or column named with an SQL reserved word is quoted in the SQL: api({at:'schema'}) reserved_word_names.
